html:
SMTO-CTX-0020 — The AI model's reply size is set larger than the model can handle

GUID: c1565527-9bbf-4965-8378-63726174c6b9
Slug: reserved-output-exceeds-context
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • Every request to an AI model has a total size limit. SMTO is set to save so much of that space for the model's answer that nothing is left for your request, so it couldn't send anything to the model.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the model you use (for example Main), and expand Limits and recovery. Output allowance and Context ceiling, the two numbers in conflict, are set there.
  2. Make Output allowance much smaller than Context ceiling, for example one quarter of it, or leave Context ceiling blank so SMTO uses the model server's real size. Then select Save Main (or the Save button for the model you changed). The model needs room for your request as well as for its answer.
  3. Select Check saved model on the same card. This confirms the model server is reachable and shows whether it accepts the new limits.
  4. Start a new task instead of resuming the old one. Tasks that already started keep the model limits they began with, so only new tasks use your change.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model shows its checks passing and a new task gets replies from the model.

If it still fails

  • The model server itself may offer less room than expected. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server or SMTO. Don't change unrelated timeouts or limits to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model client rejected its configuration because the output reservation (max_tokens) is greater than or equal to the effective context window (the configured ceiling or the window actually served by the endpoint), leaving no room for input.

What this means

  • Output reservation is greater than or equal to the effective context window, leaving no positive allowance for the required input. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • Output reservation is greater than or equal to the effective context window, leaving no positive allowance for the required input.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the captured output reservation with the effective served window, not an advertised training maximum.

How to fix it

  • In Settings > Setup > Model routing, open the affected model role's Limits and recovery and set Output allowance (max_tokens) well below Context ceiling, or clear Context ceiling to use the server's measured capacity; also confirm the endpoint actually serves the expected context length. Changes apply to new tasks; a resumed run keeps its saved context window, so start a new task instead of resuming.
  • Select a compatible model context profile and reduce the intended output reservation to leave room for input. Start a new task if changing a captured model setting; this does not shrink preserved results in an existing run.
  • Reduce the output reservation enough to leave room for the intended input within the real model context window. Start a new task to capture this setting.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Maximum Completion Tokens: model-configuration / max_completion_tokens. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The output reservation is smaller than the effective window and the complete input also passes preflight.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
